summary: Forest Service steel tower built 1951 on Albert Mountain; the register says 40 ft and the Forest Service 55 ft, and the top cab is normally locked while the stairs give views.

access.note: Reached by a moderate hike of about half a mile one way from a small gravel parking area on Forest Service Road 67. Vehicle access closes for a seasonal period from December 31 to April 1.

visit.trail_note: Stairs give views; the top cab is normally locked. A June 2010 visit report marked the stairs as not in good order.

events.note: Log lookout cabin on Albert Mountain, as early as 1942.
Steel tower built by the U.S. Forest Service on the summit, to replace abandoned towers and provide fire detection for the Coweeta Hydrologic Laboratory.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register.
Visit report: tower appears to have been abandoned for some time; nearly all equipment gone.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register describes a 40-foot steel tower and the Forest Service gives 55 feet. The story reports both. Facts use the Forest Service figure, 55 ft (16.8 m), because it is the agency's own page.
The register describes a 14x14-foot live-in cab with catwalk. Another site describes an L4 cab with a hip metal roof. Both are reported in the story.
The register names only a wooden tower on Standing Indian Mountain. The Forest Service names abandoned towers on Big Pinnacle and Standing Indian mountains. Both are reported.

notes_for_editor: Condition comes from a June 2010 register visit report; no dated current-condition source was found beyond the Forest Service recreation page (last updated July 8, 2025), which covers access only. The WillhiteWeb page is undated. Record elevation 1559.1 m matches the register's 5,115 ft; the Forest Service says about 5,200 ft and WillhiteWeb 5,220 ft, not used. No notable fires found in sources read. The 2010 visitor's name is omitted. Height 55 ft converted to 16.8 m.
